costGuide.title: SEAT CRVC Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a SEAT CRVC engine typically takes 12-16 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour and ECU coding requirements when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: The SEAT CRVC engine replacement cost is heavily influenced by the condition of the turbochargers and the extent of carbon buildup on the intake valves. Additionally, because this is a complex V6 architecture, labour time for removal and reinstallation is higher than for inline-four alternatives. failures.title: SEAT CRVC Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Water Pump & Thermostat Housing Leaks
items.whatHappens: The plastic composite housing of the water pump and thermostat assembly is prone to developing micro-fractures under repeated heat cycling. This leads to slow, often unnoticed coolant loss. If ignored, the SEAT CRVC engine can overheat, potentially warping the cylinder heads or blowing the head gasket.
items.repairVsReplace: A straightforward repair if caught early. Replacing the housing assembly is far cheaper than a full SEAT CRVC engine replacement, though it requires moderate labour time due to its location.

items.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves
items.whatHappens: As a direct-injection (TFSI) engine, fuel is sprayed directly into the cylinder, meaning it does not wash over the back of the intake valves. Over time, oil vapour from the PCV system bakes onto the valves, restricting airflow. This causes rough idling, hesitation, and a noticeable drop in power.
items.repairVsReplace: Resolved through professional walnut blasting or chemical cleaning. It does not require engine removal, but neglecting it can lead to long-term performance degradation.

items.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear
items.whatHappens: Early builds of this V6 TFSI family can experience timing chain tensioner wear or guide degradation. This presents as a distinct metallic rattling noise on cold starts. If the chain stretches excessively or skips a tooth, it can cause catastrophic valve-to-piston interference.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, a timing chain kit replacement is viable. However, if the chain has jumped time, a full SEAT CRVC engine replacement is the only reliable solution.

failures.goodYearsLine: Later revisions of the CRVC and broader 3.0L V6 TFSI family have seen improved water pump materials and updated timing chain guides, significantly reducing the frequency of these issues in post-2020 builds .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the SEAT CRVC
variants.intro: The CRVC is a Specific engine code, representing the 3.0-litre turbocharged V6 petrol variant within the broader Volkswagen Group TFSI family. It is most commonly confused with the lower-displacement 2.0 TSI engines (such as the CZPB or DKZA) found in standard Ateca and Tarraco models, or with Audi-specific 3.0 TFSI codes (like the CREA or CRBD) that share the same core architecture but feature different ECU mapping and accessory layouts. The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible near the oil filter housing or on the front timing cover. It will also be explicitly listed in section D.2 of your V5C logbook.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement SEAT CRVC - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used SEAT CRVC can be a viable budget option for high-spec SUVs, provided it comes with documented proof of strict adherence to service intervals and evidence that the water pump assembly and timing chain have been recently inspected or replaced. The primary risk is hidden carbon buildup or impending coolant leaks from age-related plastic degradation. Learn more about sourcing used engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A properly reconditioned SEAT CRVC is the recommended choice for most owners. A reputable rebuild will replace the vulnerable plastic thermostat housing, renew all external gaskets, and professionally clean the intake valves, effectively resetting the engine's reliability clock for another 100,000 miles. Explore reconditioned engines.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples or vehicles where the timing chain has failed and caused secondary internal damage. An upgraded rebuild should include revised water pump assemblies, updated timing components, and a thorough inspection of the turbocharger systems. See options for rebuilt engines.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Our network of vetted UK specialists offers comprehensive supply and fit packages for the SEAT CRVC, complete with nationwide delivery, robust warranty coverage, and necessary ECU coding. Check our supply and fit services.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: SEAT Ateca and Tarraco models equipped with the 3.0L TFSI typically hold values between £15,000 and £35,000 . With reconditioned replacement costs starting around £3,500, the investment represents a sensible fraction of the vehicle's overall value, making engine replacement a highly rational and financially sound decision compared to writing off a high-spec, modern SUV.
